title: [D6 Orchestration] Assessment persistence as typed rows with citation joins
summary: sql/migrations/0018_assessments.sql adds six analytical-layer tables — the assessment, the (assessment, evidence, role) citation join, gaps, evidence-package patterns, the retrieval trace and the disclosure record — and helena.orchestration.AssessmentStore writes them from deterministic code, one row per agent run, revalidating the request/outcome pair before anything is written. A typed failure is a row carrying the failure and no verdict. helena.budgets.model_prices reads a new, deliberately empty [model_prices] table from config/policy.toml so the derived monetary cost is a column that is NULL rather than a figure that was invented.
assumption_validated: That an agent's whole output fits typed, queryable columns with citation joins and no opaque document — validated positively and by execution: a real routed pass (scripted OpenAI-compatible endpoint, real router, real writer) stores as two rows whose every field is the in-process outcome's, the citation join resolves to a row in helena_reference_analyst_evidence in one SQL join, the verdict is split_part(classification, '.', 1) rather than a stored column, and the counts on the assessment row reconcile with the rows in the retrieval trace. Also validated negatively where it matters: the write ordering had a real bug (the endpoint-host check ran after child rows were written, so a refusal left orphans) and a cross-test contamination failure found it.
makes_buildable: Task 44 (ephemeral state and re-run recovery) gets its key already minted and already idempotent: assessment_id is a digest over (tenant, sensor, context_id, context_version, emitter, trigger) — task 44's own (context reference, version, trigger) plus the identity — a re-run upserts its own row, and the writer deletes a run's child rows before writing them so a second run that cites less does not leave the first run's citations standing. Task 45 (assessment replay) gets the stored versioned inputs: nine version columns under helena.versions.VersionSet's own field names plus model_requested, the four granted budgets as numbers, the endpoint host read off the run's own disclosure ledger, and the citations, gaps, patterns, trace and disclosures as rows. It also inherits ONE UNOWNED GAP, stated in helena.orchestration and ADR-0033 §7: the escalation is not stored and its thresholds_version reaches no row, so the routing of a pass is replayable only for a deployment whose thresholds have not moved. Task 46/47 (the sink and emission) get the join key for concept/03's one-message-per-terminal-outcome rule — the two rows of one pass share (tenant, sensor, context_id, context_version) — and a schema in the analytical layer, which helena.migrations.MAY_READ lets read both signal and reference. Task 48 (metrics) gets latency, tokens, retries, cache-hit-versus-live-query and derived cost as typed columns to aggregate rather than a document to parse.

verification.detail: 1643 passed in 529 s, full suite, no skips. 27 of them are tests/test_assessments.py and every one runs against a real RisingWave 3.0.3: the migration is applied by the real runner, the rows are written by the real writer through psycopg and read back with SQL, and the citation join is executed against helena_reference_analyst_evidence. One test drives a scripted OpenAI-compatible endpoint on the loopback interface through helena.orchestration.assess and then the store, so the object the router returns is the object the assertions read out of the engine. Two existing tests were updated for reasons stated in the commit and below, not to make them pass: tests/test_enriched.py asserted the enriched context was the ONLY analytical object (it is now the only analytical object that READS anything, which is the layer-boundary property it was checking), and tests/test_orchestration.py's no-module-state check used ast.literal_eval, which cannot evaluate CHILD_TABLES (a tuple of the table-name constants) — it now rejects Dict/List/Set/comprehension/Call nodes anywhere in a module-level assignment, which is strictly what 'no mutable module-level object' means.

escalations.detail: A `[model_prices]` TABLE WAS ADDED TO config/policy.toml AND IT SHIPS EMPTY. Task 36 escalated the derived monetary cost and named this increment as its owner ('task 43 should add the column, the price table and the version of that table it records'), and the task's own step list names 'derived cost'. What is built is the derivation, the column, the currency and the recorded price-table version; what is NOT built is a price, because a model's price is an external fact and nothing in this repository knows what the configured endpoint charges — `concept/instruction.md` §0's 'check the artifact, not the page'. An unpriced model stores NULL in all three money columns, NULL means 'not priced' and not 'free', and this is the one table in that file whose absent entry is not a startup error (a threshold nobody chose is a silent default that changes what the system does; a price nobody knows changes only whether a column can be filled in). Half a price is still refused. Flagged because it is a new config surface and because a deployment that fills it in changes what a stored assessment says it cost.

THE ESCALATION RECORD IS NOT STORED AND NO REMAINING TASK OWNS IT. `Assessment.escalation` is computed on every pass — it is what routed — and the task's step list does not name a table for it, so none was invented. It is recomputable from the projection under the recorded `policy_version`, but its `thresholds_version` lives on the `Escalation` and not on the `AgentRequest`, so it reaches no column: a replay reproduces the routing only for a deployment whose thresholds have not moved. Task 45 (assessment replay) is the first thing that cannot proceed without it. The shape it needs is a typed row per pass with the escalating candidates as join rows, which is the same shape as the citations. Stated in helena.orchestration's 'what is deliberately not here' and ADR-0033 §7.

invariant_conflicts.step: Create the assessment table with typed columns: ... verdict and classification ...
invariant_conflicts.detail: THERE IS NO `verdict` COLUMN. The verdict is the root of the classification and helena.taxonomy already refuses a path whose root is not its first segment, so a stored column would be a second copy of a fact that cannot disagree in the model and can in a table — which `concept/instruction.md` §2 rejects in the same words it uses for version constants. This is the reading helena.enrichment.EnrichmentEvidence.verdict, helena.contracts.v1.AgentResult.root and sql/migrations/0017 already took, so a column here would also have made the assessment schema disagree with the evidence schema about the same question. In SQL it is `split_part(classification, '.', 1)`, and tests/test_assessments.py asserts that against the engine rather than describing it.

deferred: THE ESCALATION RECORD. See the escalation above — it is the one thing this increment leaves that nothing else claims.

PROPOSED CLAIMS. `AgentResult.proposed_claims` is written nowhere. `concept/07` makes an agent's claim about infrastructure a proposal that deterministic code validates and writes, and where it is written is the findings table, which does not exist in any migration. Its citations are deliberately NOT folded into the assessment's citation rows — `AgentResult.evidence_ids` includes them and `AgentResult.citations` does not, and using the wider set would make the verdict look as though it cited a proposal's evidence. Asserted by a test.

THE COMPOSITION RULE'S DECISION. `Analysis.decision` — proposed versus permits, with the findings that constrained it — is not stored. `concept/07` keeps inference append-only so it is a second record beside the verdict rather than an edit of it, and it carries its own findings list: the same shape and the same missing table as the proposals above. The stored `classification` is what the MODEL said, which is the half that is append-only and correct on its own.

REFUSED RETRIEVALS. `Analysis.retrievals` holds the turns the tool layer refused and `helena.contracts.v1.RETRIEVAL_OUTCOMES` has no value for one — a refusal is not a cache hit and not a live query. Task 41 recorded that turning it into a `Gap` is a decision somebody should make deliberately rather than discover, so the trace table holds `AgentResult.retrieval_trace` and nothing else.

A READ PATH. The store writes; nothing reads an assessment back into Python. Task 45 is what needs one, and it needs it validated against the `schema_version` the row recorded rather than against current code — which is a versioned reader, not a SELECT, and inventing one here would have been a shape nothing exercises.
PRUNING. Nothing is evicted and nothing bounds the growth of any of the six tables, exactly as sql/migrations/0017 says of the evidence store. `concept/08` still lists the retention horizon as open.

A `budgets_version` KEY. Task 36 expected this increment to add one to config/policy.toml with the column that reads it. It was NOT added and the four granted budget dimensions are stored as numbers instead: those are what bounded the run, where a version string is resolvable only while that file still holds the entry it names. `concept/07`'s recorded version set is nine dimensions and a budget version is not among them, so adding one would have been a tenth dimension on helena.versions.VersionSet, which every stored row carries.
lessons: AN ASSESSMENT ROW IS ONE AGENT RUN, NOT ONE PASS THROUGH THE ROUTER. Every column `concept/03` lists — cost, latency, the nine versions, the model that answered, the endpoint, the verdict, the confidence — is a property of one run, and a pass reaches one or two agents with different models, prompts, budgets and costs. A row per pass would carry two of each or lose one. The two rows of one pass share `(tenant, sensor, context_id, context_version)`, which is what D7's 'emitted once, carrying the analyst's verdict and the triage decision that led to it' joins on.

THE WRITE ORDER IS PART OF THE CONTRACT AND A TEST FOUND IT WRONG. `AssessmentStore._one` deletes and writes the child rows first and the assessment row last, so a visible assessment always has its whole citation set. Everything that can refuse — `check_exchange`, and the two-endpoint check — must therefore run BEFORE the first child insert, or a refusal leaves orphaned children. The first version computed the endpoint host inside the INSERT parameter tuple and did exactly that; it was found by a citation row surviving into the NEXT test, because RisingWave DML is asynchronous and the unflushed inserts outlived the `migrated_engine` fixture's DELETE. Two things to carry: a refusal in a writer has to be ordered against the writes, and an unflushed insert in RisingWave can cross a test boundary.

THE ENDPOINT HOST IS READ OFF THE RUN'S DISCLOSURE LEDGER, NOT OFF CONFIGURATION. `concept/07` records endpoint and model per assessment so that cross-wiring is detectable — and configuration is exactly what would be wrong in that case, so reading the column from configuration would record the lie. `Disclosure.disclosed_to` on the `model_inference` rows is the record of where bytes actually went. NULL means no prompt ever left the process, which is a different fact from a run that reached an endpoint and failed; two hosts in one ledger is this project's own bug and is loud.

NULL IS A FIFTH KIND OF ABSENCE AND MONEY IS WHERE IT MATTERS. `model_cost` NULL means 'not priced'; it does not mean free. The whole reason `[model_prices]` ships empty is that a plausible rate in an audit record is worse than an empty column — the same argument `concept/instruction.md` §2 makes about `stale`/`failed`/`missing`/`no_match`, applied to a number.

THE 'NO FREE-TEXT NOTE' PROPERTY IS THREE TESTS, AND THE THIRD IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. (1) no table or column in the whole schema is named like a note; (2) the free-text columns are a declared six and every other stored string is a closed-vocabulary token, an identifier, a digest or a version, demonstrated over a real run rather than declared; (3) NOTHING THAT BUILDS A PROMPT CAN READ A STORED ASSESSMENT — the three modules `tests/test_untrusted.py` names as the only ones that construct a `helena.agents.Message` are read as ASTs and must not name an assessment table or the store. A bounded narrative that cannot be read back is not a memory-poisoning channel; the same narrative reachable from a prompt builder is one, whatever its length limit says.

`observation` IS THIS PROJECT'S WORD FOR TRAFFIC, NOT FOR AN AGENT'S PROSE. A note-name regex over the whole schema hits `helena_signal_entity_observations`, which is a measurement table. The loose 'observations' field the agent contract refuses is refused by `extra="forbid"` and by `tests/test_contracts.py`, which is where that rule is checkable by name.

PERSISTENCE WENT INTO `helena.orchestration` RATHER THAN A NEW MODULE, and that was `tests/test_package_layout.py`'s own instruction: its comment says `orchestration` keeps 'routing, validation, persistence and replay' of `concept/03`'s component row. A new top-level module would have been a deliberate layout edit and an escalation for no gain — the store imports nothing `orchestration` did not already import except `psycopg`.
failed_approaches: Ordering every child table by `ordinal` in the test's read-back helper. The citation table has no ordinal and cannot have one: its key is `(assessment_id, evidence_id)`, because `helena.contracts.v1.AgentResult` already refuses a result that cites one evidence id twice, and a key that admitted the same evidence under two roles would let the store hold what the contract refuses. RisingWave answers an unknown ORDER BY column with 'Failed to bind expression', not with a column-not-found at parse time.

Computing the endpoint host inside the assessment INSERT's parameter tuple. It reads naturally and it puts a refusal after the child writes — see the lesson above. The symptom was a failure in a LATER test, which is the expensive kind.

`ast.literal_eval` as the no-module-state check in tests/test_orchestration.py. It was fine while every module-level constant was a literal and it fails on `CHILD_TABLES = (CITATION_TABLE, ...)`, which is immutable and is not a literal. The check is about mutability, so it is now a walk rejecting Dict/List/Set/comprehension/Call nodes; do not 'fix' it back by inlining the strings, because two copies of a table name is what the constants exist to prevent.
next_session_should_know: Task 44 is ephemeral state and re-run recovery and task 45 is assessment replay; this task built the store both of them read and write. SEVEN THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE CALL IS `orchestration.AssessmentStore(connection, prices=budgets.model_prices()).store(assessment, at=<datetime>)` and it returns the identifiers written, TRIAGE FIRST, one or two of them. `at` is required and has no default: both rows of one pass carry the same value, because they are one pass and two timestamps a fraction apart would invite a reader to order them. `prices` is required and must be a `budgets.PriceTable`. (2) THE KEY IS `orchestration.assessment_id(tenant=, sensor=, context_id=, context_version=, emitter=, trigger=)` — a sha256, no outcome in it, so a re-run rewrites its own row. Task 44's `(context reference, version, trigger)` is a subset of it. The writer DELETEs the run's five child tables before writing them; if task 44 decides a completed prior run must not be rewritten at all, that is a decision about idempotence and it changes this, deliberately. (3) THE TABLES ARE `helena_analytical_assessment` plus `_citation`, `_gap`, `_pattern`, `_retrieval`, `_disclosure`, all named by constants on `helena.orchestration` (`ASSESSMENT_TABLE`, `CHILD_TABLES`, …). They are the `analytical` layer and they read nothing; that layer was chosen because `helena.migrations.MAY_READ` lets only `analytical` read `signal` AND `reference`, which is what a view joining an assessment to its context and its evidence needs. (4) THERE IS NO `verdict` COLUMN AND NO READ PATH. The verdict is `split_part(classification, '.', 1)`. A reader belongs to task 45 and it has to validate against the `schema_version` the ROW recorded, never against current code. (5) THE ESCALATION IS NOT STORED AND NOBODY OWNS IT — the one unowned gap this increment leaves. `thresholds_version` is on the `Escalation` and on no row, so a routing replay is only sound while the thresholds have not moved. It wants a typed row per pass with the candidates as join rows. (6) `config/policy.toml` NOW HAS `[model_prices]` AND `model_prices_version`, READ BY `helena.budgets.model_prices()`. It is empty on purpose and the three money columns are NULL; NULL is 'not priced', never 'free'. `helena.policy.PRICE_KEYS` is the fourth top-level key set and all three loaders in that file accept it. (7) IF YOU ADD A COLUMN THAT HOLDS A SENTENCE, `tests/test_assessments.py::test_the_free_text_columns_of_the_assessment_schema_are_the_declared_six` FAILS AND IT IS RIGHT. Add it to `FREE_TEXT_COLUMNS` deliberately, and check `test_nothing_that_builds_a_prompt_can_read_a_stored_assessment` still holds — that is the property, not the length limit.
